answer: Each identity is planted in the orchard, and it acts only while an ember burns in its hollow. The orchard relights that ember only for a tree wearing ferrous sunk round its trunk, welded shut for good. At dusk the orchard rings every tree to count the grove, so the trees of one root must not sound as one: each new ring must out-weigh the last. A newcomer sinks ferrous of one part; a root of a thousand identities must sink ferrous weighing half a million parts. The orchard counts every ring a root ever sank, so forks inherit the tally.
